title: QUIC RFC 9000 Path Validation Datagram Floor Runtime Work Item
summary: Implement and prove the bounded RFC 9000 Section 8.2 runtime path-validation datagram floor for challenge retries, response immediacy, same-path response emission, small-packet non-discard, and anti-amplification-aware padding.
planned_changes:
- Add a shared runtime path-validation datagram builder for PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE frames.
- Keep datagrams padded to the 1200-byte RFC minimum when the path-local anti-amplification state permits it.
- Fall back to the bare path-validation frame only when the path budget does not permit the expanded datagram.
- Preserve one PATH_CHALLENGE per datagram while allowing timer-driven retries over time.
- Keep PATH_RESPONSE emission same-transition and same-path without enforcing the same-path rule as an initiator-side peer violation.
- Fill the focused RFC 9000 S8P2 requirement homes with positive, negative, and edge coverage.
verification_plan: Run the Release build, the focused S8P2 requirement-home tests, canonical SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, diff hygiene, and the full solution test suite when the focused gates pass.
out_of_scope: Preferred-address migration completion beyond existing runtime behavior.
completion_notes: Completed as a bounded runtime and requirement-home coverage slice. PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE datagram construction now shares the same 1200-byte floor and path-local anti-amplification fallback, while focused S8P2 tests prove the direct Section 8.2 behavior.
